Screen f0 data for rows without f0

Source: R/gaps.R
screen_f0_rows.Rd

Counts the rows without f0 in each token: at the start of the token, at its end, and inside it, in gaps between two samples with f0. It also counts the gaps that the time steps show, and the short runs of samples that a gap cuts off at the start or end of a token. Nothing is changed: drop_rows_without_f0() removes the rows, and the counts here say what it does with the same arguments. The app's Start page shows these counts when a file is uploaded.

Usage

screen_f0_rows(
  data,
  token = "token",
  time = "time",
  f0 = "f0",
  gap_ratio = 1.5,
  unvoiced = NULL,
  run = "voiced_run"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format: one row per f0 sample.

token, time, f0

Column names. Defaults "token", "time", "f0". time must be the real time column. f0 is the one column that decides which rows have f0.

gap_ratio

A time step longer than this many times the token's usual step is a gap. Default 1.5. Must be above 1. Inf reads gaps from rows without f0 only.

unvoiced

Values in the f0 column to read as no f0, such as -1 or c(0, -1), for a column in Hz whose tracker marks unvoiced frames this way. Default NULL: only NA counts as no f0.

run

Name of a column that marks gaps already, such as the voiced_run column drop_rows_without_f0() adds. Default "voiced_run". Used only when the column is present. NULL ignores it.

Value

A data frame with one row per token, in order of first appearance in data. Its first column holds the token and is named as the token column. The other columns are:

  • n_rows: rows of the token.

  • n_f0: rows with f0. These are the rows left after removal.

  • n_start, n_end, n_inside: rows without f0 at the start, at the end, and inside the token.

  • n_gaps: gaps from rows without f0.

  • n_gaps_time: gaps that the time steps between samples with f0 show. A gap from rows usually shows here too, as a long step, but not in a token whose usual step is more than one frame (see Details). Always 0 when the grid is not regular.

  • frag_start, frag_end: samples in short runs cut off at the start and end (see Details).

Attributes:

  • summary: a named integer vector of counts over the whole file: rows, tokens, rows_f0, rows_without_f0, unvoiced (rows read as no f0 through unvoiced), start and start_tokens, end and end_tokens, inside, gaps and gap_tokens (gaps from rows), gaps_time and gaps_time_tokens (gaps from time steps, as in n_gaps_time), gaps_time_only and gaps_time_only_tokens (gaps from time steps with no rows without f0 in them, and the tokens with one), gaps_run and gaps_run_tokens (gaps that only the run column marks), no_f0_rows and no_f0_tokens (tokens with no f0), no_time (rows without f0 that cannot be placed, as they or the token's samples with f0 have no time), rows_after and tokens_after (left after removal), run_tokens and max_run (tokens whose voiced_run would go above 1, and its highest value), few_tokens (tokens left with 1 or 2 samples), short_runs, short_runs_start, short_runs_end, short_rows, short_tokens, short_tokens_start, short_tokens_end and short_tokens_both (short edge runs, their samples, and the tokens with one, at the start, at the end, or at both ends), rows_after_short (rows left after removal with min_run = 3), repeated_tokens (tokens with a repeated time, as in repeated_time), other_step_tokens (tokens set aside for their 2-unit steps, as in other_step), and edge_tokens and edge_rows (tokens with f0 whose first or last row has no f0, and all their rows). The voiced_run column that drop_rows_without_f0() adds marks gaps + gaps_time_only + gaps_run gaps. A token can end with two short runs, so short_runs can be more than short_tokens_start + short_tokens_end.

  • grid: a list with the time-step details. regular is TRUE when gaps were read from the time steps (in the tokens not set aside). step is the file's usual step and common is TRUE when most tokens share it. ambiguous counts steps between 1.25 and 1.75 times the usual step, nonincreasing counts steps of 0 (repeated times), and resolution is how finely the times are written. units is TRUE when the times are written to the step itself, so steps were read in whole units of resolution. off_unit then counts the steps that are not exactly one unit, and units_ok is TRUE when they are at most 1% of the steps. n_steps counts the steps judged, n_tokens_read the tokens whose steps can be read, repeated and repeated_tokens the tokens with a repeated time, other_step and other_step_tokens the tokens set aside for their 2-unit steps, n_gaps_rows the gaps from rows, and n_gaps_time the steps above gap_ratio times the usual step, regular or not. why gives the reasons the grid is not regular, as sentences named "no_steps", "ambiguous", "nonincreasing" (every token has a repeated time), "set_aside" (every token is set aside, some for their 2-unit steps), "units" (times written to the step, but more than 1% of the steps are not exactly one unit) and "resolution" (times written too coarsely). It is empty for a regular grid.

  • equal_rows: TRUE when there are at least two tokens and all have the same number of rows. A single token is not counted, so that one token of frame data is not taken for resampled points.

  • stretch: a list. warn is TRUE when equal_rows is TRUE and some token with f0 has no f0 in its first or last row. n_rows is the number of rows each token has (NA unless equal_rows), n_tokens the number of tokens with f0 that have no f0 in their first or last row, and factor the least stretch of such a token on the axes from the first f0 to the last, (N - 1) / (N - 2), whether or not the row is removed. warn_short and n_tokens_short say the same for the samples with f0 that min_run = 3 would remove at a token's start or end.

  • no_f0: the tokens with no f0, as text. Removal drops them entirely.

  • repeated_time: the tokens where two samples with f0 have the same time, as text. No gaps are read from their time steps.

  • other_step: the tokens set aside because more than 1 step in 8 is exactly 2 units, as text (see Details). No gaps are read from their time steps.

  • few_samples: the tokens left with 1 or 2 samples after removal, as a named integer vector of the samples left. flag_f0_tokens() flags them.

  • edge_missing: the tokens with f0 whose first or last row has no f0, as text (see Details).

  • unvoiced_suggested: a data frame with columns value (the values suggest_unvoiced() finds in the f0 column, such as 0 and -1) and rows (the rows holding each value). It has no rows when there is nothing to suggest.

  • settings: the arguments used, as a list.

Details

Rows without f0. A row has no f0 when its value in the f0 column is NA, NaN or infinite, or is one of the unvoiced values. Only this one column counts. Run zero_hz_to_na() first, so that 0 Hz counts as no f0 in Hz columns. Other 0 and negative values count as f0 unless they are listed in unvoiced: in a signed or normalised column (semitones, z-scores) they are real values.

Where they are. Rows are taken in time order within each token, whatever their order in data. A row without f0 is at the start when its time is before the token's first sample with f0, at the end when it is after the last one, and inside otherwise. A row without f0 at the same time as a sample with f0 counts as inside, but it makes no gap. A token with no f0 at all is counted apart: its rows are none of start, end or inside. A row with no time (NA) cannot be placed either. It still counts in n_rows, and in n_f0 when it has f0. A row whose token is NA belongs to a token of its own.

Gaps. A gap is a stretch inside a token with no f0. A gap from rows has one or more rows without f0 between two samples with f0. A gap from time steps is a step between two samples with f0 that is more than gap_ratio times the token's usual step. Gaps from time steps are read only when the time steps form a regular grid. Then the same gaps show whether or not the rows without f0 are still in the data, for tokens whose usual step is one frame. (In a token where every other frame has no f0, the usual step is two frames, so once those rows are removed the steps show no gap.) The attribute grid says whether the grid is regular, and why not. Samples timed at each glottal pulse are not regular. Give the real time column, never a *_t01, *_tseq or *_tbound axis: those restart or change step at every segment.

The default gap_ratio = 1.5 already means "one frame or more missing": a gap of one frame doubles the step, and 1.5 leaves room for jitter and floating-point noise in the times.

Times written to the step. When the times are written about as finely as the step, as for a 10 ms grid written to 2 decimals (0.01, 0.02, ...), the steps are read in whole units of 0.01: a step of 0.02 or more is a gap. This needs at least 99% of the steps to be exactly one unit. A true step that is not a whole number of units fails this, such as 12.5 ms or 7.5 ms written to 2 decimals: rounding gives steps of 0 or 0.02 in a regular pattern, not gaps. So does a file with more than 1 gap in 100 steps, as the two cannot be told apart. Times written more coarsely than the step, such as a 25 ms grid written to 2 decimals, give no gaps from the time steps. A true step within 1% of the unit, such as 10.05 ms written to 2 decimals, gives too few 2-unit steps to be told from real gaps, so write the times to at least 3 decimals when the step is not exactly 10 ms.

Tokens set aside. No gaps are read from the time steps of these tokens. Their gaps from rows still count, and the other tokens are read as usual.

  • A token where two samples with f0 have the same time: the samples are not one series of frames. The attribute repeated_time lists these tokens.

  • With times written to the step, a token where at least 2 steps, and more than 1 in 8, are exactly 2 units (0.02): its frames are probably a little more than one unit apart, as for 12.5 ms frames among 10 ms ones. A 10 ms token with that many gaps is set aside too, as the two cannot be told apart. The attribute other_step lists these tokens.

A sample with f0 but no time leaves a hole in the time steps. On a regular grid its neighbours are then two steps apart, which reads as a gap.

Gaps an earlier removal marked. When the data already have a run column (voiced_run, from an earlier drop_rows_without_f0() or from F0 Extraction), a change in its value inside a token is a gap too. This keeps the gaps from rows removed earlier, which the time steps cannot show on a grid that is not regular. run = NULL ignores the column.

Short edge runs. A run is a stretch of samples with f0 between two gaps, or between a gap and the start or end of the token. A run of 1 or 2 samples that a gap cuts off at the start or end of a token is often a tracking error in the silence. It holds the token's first or last f0, so it sets where the 0-1 time axes start or end, whether or not the rows without f0 are removed. frag_start and frag_end count these samples: those before the token's first run of at least 3 samples, and those after its last. A token with no run that long has none. drop_rows_without_f0(min_run = 3) removes them.

Equal row counts. When every token has the same number of rows N, as after resampling to N points, and a token's first or last row has no f0, removing that row leaves the token with fewer than N points. The time axes that run from the first f0 to the last (token_t01, <tier>_t01 and the models' per-token rescale) start or end such a token one point in whether or not the row is removed, so its points sit off the N-point grid, stretched by at least (N - 1) / (N - 2), 5% for 21 points. time_prop is used as it is and keeps the grid. The attribute stretch records this case, and the same for the short edge runs that min_run = 3 removes, which do move the first or last f0.

Tokens missing an end point. A token with f0 whose first or last row has no f0 is missing an end point. When every token has N rows, such a token cannot have N points over the part with f0. The attribute edge_missing lists these tokens, and the summary counts them and their rows. They are counted for any data, but matter most when every token has the same number of points, as after resampling.

Values that may mark no f0. Some trackers write 0 or a value such as -1 for unvoiced frames, in a column zero_hz_to_na() does not pick. The attribute unvoiced_suggested gives the values suggest_unvoiced() finds in the f0 column, and the rows that hold each. It is read from the column as it is, before unvoiced, so it stays the same once the values are passed to unvoiced.

See also

drop_rows_without_f0() to remove the rows; zero_hz_to_na() to run first; suggest_unvoiced() for values that may mark no f0; flag_f0_tokens() to flag the tokens with an issue; trim_to_voiced() and flag_f0_gaps().

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  token = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 10),
  time  = rep(0.005 + 0.01 * (0:9), 2),
  f0    = c(NA, 200, 202, NA, NA, 206, 208, 209, NA, NA,
            NA, NA, 181, 183, 185, 187, 188, NA, 190, NA))
scr <- screen_f0_rows(df)
scr
#>   token n_rows n_f0 n_start n_end n_inside n_gaps n_gaps_time frag_start
#> 1     a     10    5       1     2        2      1           1          2
#> 2     b     10    6       2     1        1      1           1          0
#>   frag_end
#> 1        0
#> 2        1
attr(scr, "summary")[c("rows_without_f0", "start", "end", "inside")]
#> rows_without_f0           start             end          inside 
#>               9               3               3               3 
attr(scr, "grid")$regular
#> [1] TRUE
# A gap cuts off 2 samples at the start of token a, and 1 at the end of b
scr[c("token", "frag_start", "frag_end")]
#>   token frag_start frag_end
#> 1     a          2        0
#> 2     b          0        1
# Tokens whose first or last row has no f0
attr(scr, "summary")[c("edge_tokens", "edge_rows")]
#> edge_tokens   edge_rows 
#>           2          20 
attr(scr, "edge_missing")
#> [1] "a" "b"
